Strait of Hormuz disruption.background: The Strait connects the Persian Gulf with the Gulf of Oman. Its importance to oil and LNG trade makes potential restrictions a global energy supply risk. The historical throughput figure measures exposure, not a closure.
timeline: EIA records annual oil flows through the route.
EIA estimates average oil throughput of 20.9 million barrels per day.
chain: Reduced accessible energy supply or higher transport risk
Higher crude oil and fuel costs
Higher import bills and business input costs
Possible inflation and pressure on margins
macro: Energy importers may face weaker trade balances.
Commodity exporters may benefit from higher prices if their own shipments remain accessible.
Monetary policy responses depend on inflation persistence and domestic demand.
industries: Higher prices; supply and refining risks

Red Sea shipping crisis.background: Security threats to commercial shipping in the Red Sea from late 2023 prompted carriers to divert vessels around southern Africa, lengthening voyages between Asia and Europe.
timeline: UNCTAD reports Suez transits down 70% against its mid-December 2023 comparison.
UNCTAD publishes Review of Maritime Transport 2024.
chain: Diversions around the Cape of Good Hope
Longer voyages and reduced effective shipping capacity
Higher freight, insurance and inventory costs
Potential consumer price and margin pressure
macro: Trade delivery delays can interrupt production.
Import price pass-through depends on contracts and competition.
industries: Higher voyage costs; possible freight revenue gains

Russia–Ukraine war.background: Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022 disrupted trade and production in important energy, grain and fertilizer markets. Sanctions and uncertainty also altered trade patterns.
timeline: Russia launches its full-scale invasion of Ukraine.
World Bank publishes commodity outlook forecasting wheat price growth above 40% for 2022.
chain: Energy, grain and fertilizer price pressure
Higher food and industrial input costs
Potential inflation and changes in trade balances
macro: Food and energy importers may face higher import bills.
Commodity exporters may gain from higher prices.
Household purchasing power may decline when wages lag inflation.
industries: Natural gas and fertilizer feedstock exposure
